Subject: MSA redlines: insurance naming, timing, and COI routing for HelioWorks

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA redlines. Legal flagged the insurance section: before we finalize, procurement needs to confirm the COI delivery timeline and exact additional-insured wording so we can close the order form. Quick asks: 

- Can Aegis confirm they can issue a COI that names HelioWorks as Additional Insured with the exact wording in redline #5 ("HelioWorks and its affiliates")?
- What is the earliest you can provide the COI after counter-signature? We usually request 3–5 business days; will that work?
- Are there any carrier-level endorsements needed (e.g., CG 20 10) or will the certificate + policy excerpt suffice?

Attached: Helio_MSARedlines_v3.pdf (redlined MSA).

If it helps, Kimberly is on copy for procurement timing; Rishi will weigh in for the claims-made vs occurrence question. Goal: get certificate delivered and uploaded to the contract record before DocuSign completion so we can hit the July 1 start.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: insurance naming, timing, and COI routing for HelioWorks

Hi Mina / Liam —

Thanks — Aegis can issue the COI with Additional Insured language. Two notes: 

1) We can include the naming exactly as requested ("HelioWorks and its affiliates") on the certificate holder line and in a standard endorsement.
2) Standard turnaround for issuing a COI after we receive fully executed MSA is 48 business hours; if a carrier endorsement is required (CG 20 10), lead time can extend to 3–5 business days while we obtain the endorsement from the insurer.

I've attached a draft certificate for your review (Aegis_Certificate_HelioWorks_COI.pdf). If that draft looks right we can queue it for issuance the moment you send the signed MSA.

Attachment: Aegis_Certificate_HelioWorks_COI.pdf

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: insurance naming, timing, and COI routing for HelioWorks

Thanks Aegis — and thanks Mina for flagging. Two quick clarifications from procurement/legal side: 

- Rishi: legal preference is occurrence coverage where available; if HelioWorks' carrier only offers claims-made we need a six-month tail or a retroactive date to the contract start. Please advise whether the draft MSA redline we provided (v3) is acceptable with a claims-made carve if we add a tail endorsement.

- Mina / Liam: procurement needs the COI on file prior to the first invoice. If Aegis can commit to 48 business hours post-signature for a standard COI we can proceed; if endorsements add lead time, please give a calendar estimate so we can update the order form timeline and inform Finance.

Action items: 
1) Aegis: confirm if CG 20 10 endorsement is available or if equivalent wording will be endorsed on their policy.
2) Rishi: confirm acceptance of claims-made + tail vs requiring occurrence.
3) Mina: if we get an ETA for the endorsement, I'll update the DocuSign timeline.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Aegis Insurance (COI team) <coi@aegis-ins.com>, Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@helioworks.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: insurance naming, timing, and COI routing for HelioWorks

Kimberly / Mina —

Quick legal read: we can accept claims-made if the carrier provides either: (a) an extended reporting period (tail) of at least 12 months after termination, or (b) a retroactive date that precedes the contract effective date by the same duration as Redwood's operational exposure (typical ask ~12 months). Occurrence policies remain preferred but not mandatory here given HelioWorks' market. 

On endorsements: CG 20 10 (Additional Insured — Owners, Lessees or Contractors) is standard and preferred. If Aegis cannot supply CG 20 10, we will accept insurer-issued equivalent endorsement language that specifically names "HelioWorks and its affiliates" and provides ongoing additional insured status for ongoing operations.

Procurement timeline note: if Aegis needs 3–5 business days for endorsement issuance, procurement should expect a 1-week slippage on the DocuSign and invoicing timeline. Please confirm and I'll sign off on the MSA once the COI/endorsement ETA is posted.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
